title: Nonlinear associations between physical activity, sleep quality, and psychological distress in university students: a cross-sectional interpretable machine learning study.
summary: The paper reports a specific population association and test performance. Its spline analysis directly evaluates the shape; do not interpret the result as causal or as an optimal exercise prescription.
ai_technology: XGBoost with SHAP interprets nonlinear feature associations; a group-held-out evaluation separates classes in the stated dataset.
organization: China University of Mining and Technology; Beijing Union University; Shandong University of Aeronautics

evidence.tested: The paper reports a specific population association and test performance. Its spline analysis directly evaluates the shape; do not interpret the result as causal or as an optimal exercise prescription. The class-held-out test and conventional comparators support internal evaluation; one university and cross-sectional self-report limit external and causal claims.
evidence.unknown: nonlinear associations between physical activity and distress, with XGBoost/SHAP and group-held-out evaluation; the cross-sectional finding is associative, not causal.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost with SHAP interprets nonlinear feature associations; a group-held-out evaluation separates classes in the stated dataset.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
